extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to Remote Code Execution. The query parameter `username` (source: `async def read_root(username=None)` at line 8) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string passed to `Environment().from_string(...).render()` at line 14. An attacker controlling the `username` query parameter (e.g. `/?username={{ 7*7 }}` or a payload such as `{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}`) can execute arbitrary Python code on the server, read server-side objects (e.g. `{{ config }}`), and fully compromise the application. The fix is to pass user data as a render context variable to a fixed template (as shown in the commented 'safe implementation' at line 17) rather than embedding it in the template source.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The user-controlled `username` query parameter is embedded verbatim into the Jinja2 template at line 14 — the `Environment()` created at line 11 has no `autoescape=True` — and the resulting string is returned to the browser via `HTMLResponse(content=output)` at line 19 with content-type `text/html` and no output encoding or sanitization. An attacker can craft a link such as `/?username=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` that executes arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Fix by enabling autoescaping and rendering user data as a template context variable (line 17 pattern).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
